title: Two Work Packages write the same three story files and three fragments for legacy RWB-E1-064 on rwb-source-data
source: Work Package files _work/msr/wp/B-P1-02.md and _work/msr/wp/B2-P1-001.md (both list the same 'Write only' paths 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data (Source data)/RWB P1 E1064 APP ... v1.md, ... CON ... - contract v1.md and ... OPS ... - deployment v1.md, and the same three fragment paths _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P1-E1064-APP.json, -CON.json and -OPS.json); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (one slice per work type for legacy RWB-E1-064: RWB-P1-E1064-APP, RWB-P1-E1064-CON, RWB-P1-E1064-OPS, plus RWB-ITG-E1064-ITG); _work/msr/status.json (B-P1-02 RUNNING 1 try, B2-P1-001 RUNNING 2 tries); _work/msr/editlog/B-P1-02.md
section: Whole story file set of RWB-E1-064 on rwb-source-data; fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P1-E1064-APP.json, RWB-P1-E1064-CON.json, RWB-P1-E1064-OPS.json
description: The plan carries one slice per work type for legacy RWB-E1-064 on rwb-source-data (the application, the contract baseline and the deployment), but two Work Packages of the run name them: B-P1-02, which lists RWB-E1-064 beside RWB-E1-065, E1-066, E1-067 and E2-010 with fanout 5 and wrote the E1064 key as part of that fanout, and B2-P1-001, which names the same three story files and the same three fragments alone with fanout 0. Both were RUNNING at the same time (B-P1-02 1 try, B2-P1-001 2 tries), so a second write of the three paths would overwrite a complete deliverable of a live worker rather than add content: the three files present in the tree are 54,534, 56,101 and 43,013 bytes with their 19 sections, their 20 metadata rows, their eight criteria each and their section 12 tables, and their six missing values are already registered once as CG-B-P1-02-E1064-101, -201 and -301 with ASM-B-P1-02-E1064-101, -201 and -301. Under root AGENTS.md rule 1 the existing artefacts are kept and this Work Package registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding, so the numbering of the Gap Register and of the Assumption Register is not allocated twice for one slice at step D1. No story content is missing because of it; the risk is a second set of CG and ASM numbers citing the same six values, and an overwrite that loses the citation set the delivered files use.
evidence: B-P1-02.md 'Write only' block: the three RWB P1 E1064 story paths and the three RWB-P1-E1064 fragment paths; B2-P1-001.md 'Write only' block: the same six paths; editlog/B-P1-02.md 'Files written' list: the same six paths, written by that execution, with 16 gap rows and 16 assumption rows of its own; gaps/B-P1-02.jsonl: CG-B-P1-02-E1064-101, -201, -301, the six placeholders the three files cite, all resolving to a row; assumptions/B-P1-02.jsonl: the three matching ASM rows; status.json: B-P1-02 RUNNING (1 try), B2-P1-001 RUNNING (2 tries); split_plan.json: one slice each for RWB-P1-E1064-APP, -CON, -OPS
proposed: Keep one Work Package per story slice in the plan generator: remove RWB-E1-064 from B-P1-02's fanout list, or retire B2-P1-001 for this key. At step D1, number the three rows of CG-B-P1-02-E1064-101, -201 and -301 once and allocate no second set for B2-P1-001; add a plan-uniqueness check to checks/run_all.py that fails when two WP 'Write only' blocks name the same output path, as the B2-P1-014 finding already asks.
